panels.observation: Source P1 Panel 1 caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' is used verbatim as narration. Because it names Dr. Ananya, the reader knows who greets the patients. It depends on no earlier text.

Meera's source line is verbatim, split at the ellipsis into two balloons ('Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...' / 'I wish everything were easier to manage!'). Same speaker, no turn skipped. The ringing phone and registers in the scene give the list its premise.
Ananya's line is verbatim. 'the rest' refers back to Meera's paperwork list in 01-2, which comes just before it, so the referent stays.
Caption verbatim. The label 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' is a manga supplement naming the product the source panel shows. It reads after the caption and does not change meaning.
Ananya's 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' is verbatim. 'here' is backed by the laptop setup established in 02-1.

Meera's 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' is verbatim. The opening 'And' continues Ananya's 02-2 line, which comes just before it with no other speaker in between. The WELBUK CARE label is a supplement.
Ananya's 'One team. Better coordination.' is verbatim and sums up 02-2 and 02-3. Meera only nods, with no added line.

Revised source P3 Panel 1 caption 'Ravi arrives for his visit.' is verbatim. It introduces Ravi by name after the 02-4 -> 03-1 time change. The textColumns join exactly. The phone in his right hand sets up 03-2.
Caption 'Scan to check in.' is verbatim. The imperative is clear from the QR stand introduced in 03-1, so nothing is missing.

Caption 'A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.' is verbatim. 'his' refers to Ravi from 03-1 and 03-2, and the consent tick-box in the scene shows 'consent'. The textColumns join exactly.

Caption 'His token appears on the screen.' and label 'TOKEN A-12' are verbatim and in source order (caption, then the TV label). 'His token' follows from the submitted form in 03-3. The screen is drawn blank and the token is lettered.

Nurse line 'Let's check your vitals, Ravi.' is verbatim, with speaker 'nurse' as in the source. The name is justified by the check-in form and token in 03-3 and 03-4. 'Let's check' opens the vitals beat after the time-change bridge from 03-4. No readings are shown, as the source requires. (See the issue about the shoulder-bag state.)

Caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.' and label 'RAVI · READY' are verbatim and in order. 'he' refers to Ravi. The place change to the consultation room is stated in the transition. It is set up for 04-1's greeting. (See the issue about the doctor-tablet carry-over.)
